newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH HAULIERS FILE COMPLAINT AGAINST FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH HAULIERS FILE COMPLAINT AGAINST FRANCE.

text.p: Dutch haulier organisation EVO said on Thursday it filed an official complaint against France, through the European Commission, because Paris refused to intervene in over 200 road-blocks set up by striking French truckers.
EVO's lawyers argued that the lack of intervention was in conflict with the free traffic of goods and services guaranteed in European Union treaties.
EVO, which has 36,500 member firms, said in a statement that it was taking this step because French blockades had so far cost Dutch producers and traders over 55 million guilders.
The organisation said Dutch exporters were losing three to four million guilders a day due to truckers' road blocks in France and Denmark.
"Given recent precedent, the (European) Commission is bound to intervene if it receives a complaint," it said.
EVO said it wanted all blocks on European roads lifted, adding that most insurance policies did not cover losses caused by this type of protest action.

The organisation has asked the Dutch government to provide financial compensation to businesses hit by truckers' action, and Trade Minister Anneke van Dok has confirmed she would press her French and Danish counterparts to take action to free major road arteries.
Costs to Dutch hauliers include the loss of perishable goods, re-routing costs and claims for late delivery by customers in France, Spain and Portugal.
"They also suffer direct commercial damage because customers divert business to other suppliers," EVO said.
Striking French truckers voted on Thursday to keep up their 11-day stranglehold on the French economy in defiance of French government calls to return to work after pay talks collapsed.
